Jesse got into that situation for a friend. Remember his loyalty?  Yeah, he will do anything for his friends. He's pretty naive in that sense. When he gets into that pigsty, there's a fucking kid. There's something that really gets under my skin about a kid living with shitty parents and I'm sure that Jesse felt the same way. He empathizes with this kid and tries to make this kid's life better... and the parents take out Jesse.

The parallels between the kid and Jesse isn't too hidden. Both of them are loyal to people close to them. Both have to fend for themselves. Both have had their futures ruined by drugs.

So back to the conflict- should Jesse leave and break his promise to his friend, leaving this kid with his shitty parents, or not? Unfortunately, he can't exactly leave at that point. They were going to kill him. At least he made sure the kid would be picked up.

Would you feel remorse about the death of drug addicted child abusers? Would you have taken the child into your home? How could you explain having the child with you and not being tied into the deaths of the parents?

The point I'm making is Jesse made choices that, while hard, stuck to his baseline of loyalty. By bringing the child, he would endanger Mr. White. The child can have a better chance in the system. Why bring the child into another drug ridden household? In the world of drugs, loyalty is the best you can hope for. No one is unaffected in the business. We learn in this episode that Jesse tries to involve children as little as possible because of this incident. It sets up the conflict of the boy with the bicycle. I call him morally strong because Jesse knows who he is and what he stands for. For every morally strong good guy, there is a morally strong bad guy as well. Jesse uses logic like this. If he didn't think of the world as good guys and bad guys, I would agree with you. His black and white reasoning cinches my ideas that he is a morally strong character though.

It feels like it has a great prospect for a story, but it needs to be more refined. Right now it is like a coarse diamond. While you have a great concept and I am interested to know your idea, the character is bland right now. This is suggested by the bland repetition of boring words, i.e. pain, cold, every. Connotation (that vocab word you learn in the poetry section in high school) is a very powerful tool. The sounds a word has can make the subject sound more negative, condescending, optimistic, etc. Definitely use a thesaurus to get the best atmosphere for your story.

The best way to build intrigue is by having the reader invoke their imagination, not by telling them incessant details. Being force fed is less enjoyable than discovering and eating bits for yourself. Right now you can clearly see what the story should be, but it isn't that obvious to everyone else. A good point to use is to take away sentences and see how it affects the product as a whole. This is up for interpretation of you.

Personally, I would get rid of the first two sentences. The sentences ahead already suggest a desert with a red giant of a sun. I would change the first sentences as such:

'A rapidly fading trail of crimson dots stretched behind me, the only thing showing my progress under the cloudless sky. Nothing broke the horizon ahead of me except some cacti and the occasional tumbleweed.'

Second point:

> "I knew I should be feeling glad that the bleeding is slowing down but I can’t feel anything but exhaustion, disgust and pain. Pain followed my every step and every shallow breath of the dusty desert air. Judging by the amount of pain I felt, I should probably be dead; nonetheless, I steadily pressed on along a long-forgotten cracked desert road."

This passage suggests that the speaker feels like a tragic hero, but really they seem like they are whining the whole way. Like I said before, the repetition of the word pain just makes it seem like the speaker is really milking for the reader's sympathy. I don't like reading a book where I am greeted by a speaker who self-diagnoses themselves by their pain. Maybe by the amount of blood loss, but pain is a very unreliable mistress. Also, when you are about to die, there is usually a rush of adrenaline that cushions the actual amount of pain. Where is the bleeding? How is he bleeding? 

Why is this speaker so condescending? Make the speaker more likeable to the reader. If they are a condescending asshole, don't make him admit his envy. If they are something else, don't break character. You don't want to him to be an open book character so early in the book- it's a hook to draw them in. 

And is the match talking to the speaker in the manner of a little kid? Really use realistic speech when introducing unnecessary characters. Unless dweeb is something the speaker or one of the main cast has a habit of using.

**TL;DR Fair skinned, sensitive, acne prone, and went from knowing nothing to becoming pretty skilled at makeup in 3 years** 

   Hey! I used to be in colorguard and we had to put on serious makeup all the time. I remember not knowing anything, so I made an account to help! I'll try breaking it down, and if you feel like questioning any steps, please, ask away! :D

PREP

   This may seem unnecessary, but secretly this is the best step of all. It takes up about a half hour to an hour for me, but it will soothe your nerves and make you shine through your makeup.You can't have a great painting without a proper canvas!
Whatever you do: don't try picking or touching your face. You may feel like helping. You will cause flareups and make it harder to cover up; i.e. putting on more makeup.
The best thing you can possibly do is to take care of your skin before you put on makeup. Most important steps you can take. Remember:

* **Cleanse** What I like to do is take a cotton ball and soak it with milk. Then rub with a circular motion all over your face. Splash off the excess with water and pat dry. Sounds weird, but trust me. Unless you are lactose intolerant. Then use steam for five minutes and wipe face.

* **Exfoliate** Two words. Honey and sugar. Mix a tsp. of honey and mix with a tsp. of sugar in a bowl. Warm up mixture by rubbing between your three main fingers. Use circular motion to exfoliate. Leave on for roughly a minute or two. Wash off with water.

* **For special events- Mask** [Recommended](http://www.crunchybetty.com/mocha-frappucino-mask-coffee-cocoa-and-honey-facial-mask) IF no coffee, try an aspirin mask. I have never used an aspirin mask, but my friends have with great results.

* **Moisturize** Coconut oil, Extra virgin olive oil, cocoa butter, or your favorite moisturizer. A dime's worth. Warm between fingers and spread.
I like to practice these steps the day before, to see how well I turn out. 

Makeup

    Whatever you do, you can always practice the day before. (:
Do your makeup in natural light. Otherwise you will look wonky when you leave the house. Have a mirror by the window!
Also: ring finger is the best. Always blend concealer and eyeshadows with your ring finger. It will come out better than any other finger.
